text:
leo: flipped tenant `horizon` to v2 for a tiny 3% canary at 08:17 PT. within 40s PM reported a v1 token "blip" on the routes chart. can someone check routing vs billing?

console-bot: config-change detected: tenant=horizon v2_prefer=true @2025-09-11T15:17:10Z. dashboards aggregate by billing_meter_key by default.

anya: pulling traces. router shows chosen_route=v2 for sampled reqs, but billing entries for some of the same req ids show meter_key=v1 for ~60-90s after the flip. looks like binding hasn't rehydrated in billing.

clare: our billing worker memoizes tenant->meter_key for 4m by default to reduce DB pressure. when a route flips, router uses new binding instantly but billing keeps the cached mapping until expiry.

leo: that explains the UI mismatch. PMs see stacked chart and assume v2 is failing. we need clearer signals.

rob: infra quick fix: we can emit a `tenant-binding:update` pubsub message on route flips and have billing invalidate that tenant's cache immediately. low-risk. i'll open a small PR.

anya: UX/ops quick wins: 1) add a dismissible toast on the toggle: "Route change submitted 010 billing attribution may lag ~90s due to caching" with link to docs; 2) add a chart toggle: "Show by chosen route / Show by billing key" so stakeholders can view both perspectives.

leo: also think we should surface a per-tenant metric `binding_age` (seconds since last binding refresh) and `attribution_mismatch_pct` (sampled percent where chosen_route != meter_key). that helps on-call not hit panic.

clare: agree. billing can emit last_binding_refresh_ts; analytics can compute binding_age. we can use binding_age to suppress quota alerts while >60s after a route-change.

rob: PR #6122: "emit tenant-binding:update on route toggle" opened. adds pubsub publish and a small handler in billing to invalidate memo and trigger an eager rebind. staging runbook added.

opsbot: prod-config-change: pin.ttl(horizon)=0 applied by leo @2025-09-11T15:18:20Z.

anya: short-term mitigation applied: pin TTL drop avoids sticky cross-version fallbacks during early canary. after rob's patch we should see billing alignment <10s in staging.

rob: landed in staging. billing now listens to `tenant-binding:update` and triggers rebind; added metric `last_binding_refresh_ts`. e2e verifies memo invalidation latency <5s.

clare: follow-up: add rollout guard in rollouts service: block increases past 8% until binding_age < 30s (configurable). prevents teams from ramping before billing is aligned.

leo: good idea. will we expose that as a recommended default in the console?

anya: UX: yes, show a small warning when increasing canary percent above 8% while binding_age>30s: "Recommended: wait for billing binding to refresh to avoid misleading metrics" with a "Force increase" option if needed.

rob: i'll add the guard as a soft block with override and emit an audit event when override used. small backend change + unit tests.

opsbot: runtime-flag: trace.sample_override(horizon)=100% active 20m per leo request.

leo: after patch in staging, attribution realigned in ~6s for the sampled traces. this looks promising. i'll file the RFC to formalize the toast, chart toggle, binding metrics, and rollout guard. owners: rob infra, anya UX, clare analytics.

anya: also suggest small docs update for on-call: "When route flips occur, check binding_age & attribution_mismatch_pct before rolling back solely on billing spikes."

leo: RFC filed as RFC-7022, linking PR #6122 and mock images. closing thread once RFC review done. thanks all :thumbsup:
